messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] web site still down?
parts:
It wasn’t a coincidence, but it also wasn’t solely due to the push.

Recall the way DNS works — you enter a domain into a client,
the client finds a local DNS server, asks for what IP that
domain resolves to, and then accesses that IP. A CNAME
is a redirection at the DNS level — if a domain has a CNAME
then when a DNS server requests its IP it just forwards the
request to another domain.

So if we want requests for mc-stan.org to resolve to github
then we need a CNAME on mc-stan.org. Which is what
I had set up when I went to bed last night, but it takes a long
time for that CNAME to propagate to all of the DNS servers
around the world. So by the time you pushed most of the
servers were updated and mc-stan.org was forwarding as
desired. When Dan took down the CNAME by restoring
mc-stan.org’s DNS settings nothing happened because it
will take a while for those changes to propagate.

Right now you can see the correct behavior,

> dig mc-stan.org
…
;; ANSWER SECTION:
mc-stan.org. 43200 IN CNAME stan-dev.github.io.
stan-dev.github.io. 3600 IN CNAME github.map.fastly.net.
github.map.fastly.net. 15 IN A 185.31.19.133

You request mc-stan.org, the CNAME redirects to
stan-dev.github.io. stan-dev.github.io has its own internal
CNAME that forwards to their custom DNS server that
finally resolves an IP using an alias (hence the A).
Once the CNAME on mc-stan.org (i.e. pairNIC) is gone
this will no longer work.

Ido added a CNAME text file to stan-dev.github.io. This
doesn’t affect mc-stan.org at all. What it does is it tells
github to treat all of its domains as if they were mc-stan.org,
so you can type in stan-dev.github.io it will display
“mc-stan.org” in your browser window but never contact
the pair servers.

Long story short, I was waiting for the pair CNAME to propagate
to make sure mc-stan.org correctly forwarded to github
before adding the CNAME text file back to stan-dev.github.io.

messages.author: 2c952029259d7788
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] web site still down?
parts:
I'm sorry, but you're partially mistaken - the CNAME file in GitHub also tells GitHub's web servers when they get an HTTP/1.1 Host: header line with mc-stan.org to make that go to the right page (Stan-dev's org page). Without it, even with the DNS CNAME pointing to Stan-dev.github.io, GitHub's web server would display a 404 or 500 error since it doesn't know what page to display when it gets a request for mc-stan.org...

You need both the DNS CNAME and the CNAME file in the org GH page's master branch. As for DNS propagation delay, even most caching name servers from ISPs respect your DNS refresh time / TTL which you have set reasonably low that the change would be seen within an hour. You can always check if it's a propagation issue by doing dig mc-Stan.org @ns1.pairwhatever.com to get a response from Pairnic's/ an authoritative server. I did this and saw that it was not a DNS issue, it was GitHub not recognizing the Host: header since a CNAME file was missing.

The gh-pages branch in GitHub where you have a CNAME file already is completely ignored by github pages/web servers, but the master branch's CNAME is read and used.

Cheers,
Ido

> stan-dev.github.io. 3600 IN CNAME github.map.fastly.net.

> stan-dev.github.io. stan-dev.github.io has its own internal

> finally resolves an IP using an alias (hence the A).
> Once the CNAME on mc-stan.org (i.e. pairNIC) is gone
> this will no longer work.
>
> Ido added a CNAME text file to stan-dev.github.io. This

> “mc-stan.org” in your browser window but never contact
> the pair servers.
>

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] web site still down?
parts:
> I'm sorry, but you're partially mistaken - the CNAME file in GitHub also tells GitHub's web servers when they get an HTTP/1.1 Host: header line with mc-stan.org to make that go to the right page (Stan-dev's org page). Without it, even with the DNS CNAME pointing to Stan-dev.github.io, GitHub's web server would display a 404 or 500 error since it doesn't know what page to display when it gets a request for mc-stan.org...
>
> You need both the DNS CNAME and the CNAME file in the org GH page's master branch. As for DNS propagation delay, even most caching name servers from ISPs respect your DNS refresh time / TTL which you have set reasonably low that the change would be seen within an hour. You can always check if it's a propagation issue by doing dig mc-Stan.org @ns1.pairwhatever.com to get a response from Pairnic's/ an authoritative server. I did this and saw that it was not a DNS issue, it was GitHub not recognizing the Host: header since a CNAME file was missing.

Yes, I was monitoring dig and whatsmydns — the changes had not yet propagated
by the time I went to bed. Again, I wanted to make sure pair was correctly configured
before adding the CNAME textfile to GitHub.
> The gh-pages branch in GitHub where you have a CNAME file already is completely ignored by github pages/web servers, but the master branch's CNAME is read and used.

Yes, I know. As I noted in a previous email gh-pages is leftover from when the
website was a project page.
